Leadership introduction

AIDS APAANA is a Uganda-based foundation working on HIV/AIDS awareness, fundraising and community support. Its leaders set the direction, look after the resources entrusted to the foundation, and make sure the work reaches the people who need it.

This page introduces the board, executive leadership, program leads and team. Details marked “to be added” will be completed as they are confirmed.

The foundation at a glance

Based in

Serving

Focus

Our message
End the shame & stigma

Roles and responsibilities

A clear split of responsibilities keeps decisions accountable and the work moving.

Board
  • Set the foundation’s direction and protect its mission
  • Oversee how funds and resources are managed
  • Approve key policies and annual plans
  • Review the work of executive leadership
  • Make sure the foundation meets its legal obligations
Executive leadership
  • Run daily operations and carry out board decisions
  • Report to the board on progress, finances and risks
  • Represent the foundation to partners, donors and authorities
  • Supervise program leads and staff
Program leadership
  • Plan and deliver the work in their program area
  • Track results and report on impact
  • Coordinate with communities, health partners and volunteers
  • Keep personal information private and treat everyone with dignity
Team members
  • Carry out program activities in the field and online
  • Support outreach and awareness campaigns
  • Follow the foundation’s policies on privacy and conduct
  • Share feedback and community needs with program leads

These are draft descriptions. Update them to match the foundation’s constitution and job descriptions.
